content: Currently, I start to look at the PR with the upcrossing lemmas. I have a general question, which also involves the file in mathlib. I do not understand why upcrossings are only defined for random functions (i.e. they depend on some ω. Aren't upcrossings also a concept for a deterministic function?

Ok, thanks Wojciech!

Maybe we can discuss some ideas on Friday via zoom: At the moment, times of upcrossings in Mathlib are built on hitting/hittingBtwn/lowerCrossingTimeAux/upperCrossingTime.

  1. All of these definition are pointwise in ω. They could more generally be formulated in terms of trajectories (rather than stochastic processes), i.e. ω-free.
  2. Several definitions (upperCrossingTime/lowerCrossingTime/upcrossingsBefore/upcrossings) need OrderBot. This is used in order to have a starting point for the upcrossings. Inherently, this is not needed, and could as well be replaced by defining the upcrossings starting from some fixed time.
  3. The trajectory/stochastic process is ℝ-valued, however only the (pre-)order is needed to see when the trajectory/stochastic processes is below a or above b. So, this could be generalized to [Preorder _].

The current PR builds on all of these mathlib-concepts, so it would be worthwhile to refactor the corresponding concepts in mathlib before merging this PR.
I agree that upcrossings should be defined for a function, not a process, and then used for paths of the process. Could you propose a Mathlib PR to change that?
It then becomes an analysis definition, so it should change the file, ok?

Rémy Degenne schrieb:

I agree that upcrossings should be defined for a function, not a process, and then used for paths of the process. Could you propose a Mathlib PR to change that?

Yes, I will do that. Probably there will be more than one PR, the first one is moving upcrossing etc definitions to some analysis file (getting rid of the omegas...)
